reason: The Relevance Gate's two counters now carry `conversation_id`, so a refusal can be joined to the room it refused. Before this a `no_go` said only «somewhere on Signal», and the two measures that would grade the gate against something other than its own opinion — it refused room R while she demonstrably held something for R, and a human tagged her in R within minutes of a `no_go` — were uncomputable even though both sides of the join were already in Postgres. Both series are labelled, not just the verdict one: a fail-closed no_go refuses the room exactly as a chosen one does, so a measure blind to the error series under-counts refusals by whatever the outage rate happens to be (14 of 290 over the seven days to 2026-09-16). The series stay separate — «the room was quiet» and «the gate is down» must never be one reading. Cardinality is bounded by the configured conversation roster. No behaviour change: the gate still neither reads nor writes the decision log, and no verdict changes. Nothing a member of a room can observe.
